problem: Existing object-goal navigation methods feed raw sensory features into RL and ignore hierarchical object relationships, so they overfit training scenes and generalize poorly to unseen rooms, especially for small targets. Scene-prior graphs only encode spatial co-occurrence, not parent-target dependency.
motivation: Humans find small objects by first locating larger related 'parent' objects (e.g. stove or microwave for a toaster). Object-object relations are domain-independent, so using them should generalize better than scene-specific features. Baselines reached high training SR (~90%) but far lower test SR (~35%), which suggests they memorize the training scenes.
key_idea: Encode detector output as a per-object context vector fed to a GCN over a Visual Genome knowledge graph, and shape the A3C reward with partial rewards for seeing parent objects related to the target.
insight: Replacing ResNet features with the object-centric context vector (MJOLNIR-o) raises L>=1 SR from 54.8 (MJOLNIR-r) to 65.3, and both variants beat all baselines by a large margin. Removing the context-vector concatenation layer (no g) drops SR to 59.0, so the context vector helps the graph embeddings. Training and test SR curves stay close for MJOLNIR, whereas Scene Prior reaches about 90% train SR and about 35% test SR, showing that the abstract object-centric state plus the shaped reward curbs overfitting. Note that the observation stream uses a ground-truth object detector.
method: Parent-target relation: a manually chosen set of larger parent objects per room type (kitchen, living room, bedroom, bathroom) that are spatially and semantically tied to the target objects.
Knowledge graph: nodes are the 101 AI2-THOR objects, built from Visual Genome captions with aliases pruned (e.g. armchair vs arm chairs, near vs next to) to give a cleaner adjacency matrix.
Context vector: a 5-D vector per object [detected b, xc, yc, bbox area, GloVe cosine similarity to the target], giving a 101x5 context matrix from the (ground-truth) object detector.
Contextualized Graph Network (CGN): a 2-layer GCN on node features (detection indicator + GloVe), whose output is concatenated with the context vector and passed through a third GCN layer.

Observation stream and joint embedding: MJOLNIR-r uses ResNet-18 conv features fused with the target GloVe by point-wise conv; MJOLNIR-o uses the flattened context matrix. This is concatenated with the graph embedding, fed to an LSTM and then A3C.

Reward shaping: partial reward Rp = Rt * Pr(t|p) * k (Rt=5, k=0.1) on the first sighting of each parent, taking the max over visible parents; goal reward Rt + Rp on Done with the target visible; step penalty -0.01. Pr(t|p) comes from a matrix of target-parent co-occurrence within 1 m in the training floorplans.
Training: A3C built on the SAVN code, 3M episodes, SharedAdam with lr 1e-4 and discount 0.99.

setting.backbone: ResNet-18 / GT object detector + GloVe + 3-layer GCN + LSTM + A3C (trained from scratch, ResNet-18 pretrained on ImageNet)
setting.training_data: AI2-THOR v1.0.1 offline data: first 20 of 30 floorplans per room type (80 rooms) for 3M episodes; Visual Genome captions for the knowledge graph
setting.observation: egocentric RGB; MJOLNIR-o uses ground-truth object detections (bbox, class) from the simulator, plus the target GloVe word embedding
setting.action_space: discrete low-level: MoveAhead 0.25 m, RotateLeft/Right 45°, LookUp/LookDown 30°, Done
setting.privileged: ground-truth object detector for the observation stream (MJOLNIR-o) and ground-truth object positions to build the partial reward matrix; one ablation also uses the environment's termination signal

numbers_note: AI2-THOR object-goal navigation is not in the canonical benchmark list, so it is labeled other. The split is called 'test' in the paper's Table 1 (unseen test rooms, 10 of 30 floorplans per room type).
results: MJOLNIR-o reaches 65.3 SR / 21.1 SPL (L>=1) on unseen AI2-THOR rooms, against 35.7 SR / 9.3 SPL for SAVN and about 35 SR for Baseline and Scene Prior. The abstract claims gains of 82.9% SR and 93.5% SPL over the best prior method. Using the environment stop signal raises SR to 83.1, and training converges faster with less overfitting.
limitations: MJOLNIR-o depends on a ground-truth object detector, and the parent objects and the partial reward matrix are hand-designed from simulator object positions, which limits realism.

The agent gets stuck when the target is visible but the path is blocked, and the Done action is sometimes wrongly sampled or not sampled; the environment stop signal fixes the latter but would not be available on a real robot and lengthens episodes.
Evaluated only in AI2-THOR with 4 room types and 5-6 targets per room, and with no real robot.
